description: For a repo with an Expo app. Each Expo SDK names the exact versions of React, React Native and every native module it bundles,
so Renovate moves only `expo` itself. The expo-fix workflow (.github/workflows/expo-fix.yml here, called from the app's repo)
then runs `npx expo install --fix` on the Renovate branch and commits the matching versions of everything else.
An SDK major waits on the Dependency Dashboard: tick it when there is time to build both platforms and run the e2e flows.
Expo picks these versions. A Renovate PR for one of them on its own would be reverted by `expo install --fix`.
A react-native-* library that Expo does not bundle is turned back on in the repo's own renovate.json.

packageRules.description: `expo` gets its own PR, and its range moves with it (~58.0.20 becomes ~58.0.26), so the companions follow.

An Expo SDK release, even a patch, changes native code, so it stays a PR that a person merges after building the app on both platforms; the rest of the app's npm updates merge on green checks like anywhere else.
A new Expo SDK changes React Native, the Xcode image EAS builds on, and sometimes the app's own code.
prBodyNotes: **A new Expo SDK.** Before merging: read the SDK's changelog (expo.dev/changelog), wait for the `expo-fix` commit on this branch, run `npx expo-doctor` in the app, build a development client on iOS and Android and run the Maestro flows on both. The first EAS build after the merge also moves to the SDK's Xcode image.
